basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 20.' and it opens 'Vers. 20. Quindecim cubitis altior fuit aqua super montes. Dicunt enim quidam hoc'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 20. Quindecim cubitis altior fuit aqua super montes. Dicunt enim quidam hoc historialiter fieri non potuisse sed propter aliquam significationem vel mysterium hoc scriptum esse. Aiunt enim non potuisse fieri, ut aqua crassioris naturae ad superiorem aeris partem conscenderet maxime propter | Olympum montem, cujus tanta altitudo ut nulli venti ibi flare, nullae nubes cacumen ejus valeant operire. Sed qui hoc fatentur non attendunt quia mons ipse terra est. Terram autem scimus corpulentiorem esse aqua. Ubi ergo terra gravior ascendere potuit, cur non hoc levior aqua potuerit?
